text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English poet JOHN MILTON, whose greatest works were "Paradise Lost", "Paradise Regained" and "Samson Agonistes", was born in 1608.

Australian author GEORGE BARTON was born in 1836. His best-known work was "The True Story of MARGARET CATCHPOLE". He was dismissed from his public service position after writing a satirical poem in the "Punch" magazine.
Australian stock and station agent HENRY BADGERY was born in 1840. He wrote verse under the nom de plume of YABBER JOE.
The creator of "Brer Rabbit" JOEL CHANDLER HARRIS was born in Georgia in 1848. He also created "Uncle Remus".
Australian horseman HARRY "BREAKER" MORANT was born in 1864. His execution for shooting civilian prisoners in the Boer War was the subject of a film.
American pioneer of the deep-frozen food industry CLARENCE BIRDSEYE was born in 1886.
American actor DOUGLAS FAIRBANKS JUNIOR, whose films included "The Prisoner of Zenda", "The Catherine The Great" and "Sinbad the Sailor", was born in 1909.
German operatic soprano ELISABETH SCHWARZKOPF, who was noted for her interpretations of MOZART and RICHARD STRAUS, was born in 1915.
American actor KIRK DOUGLAS, who specialised in tough, dramatic roles, was born in 1918.

Former Labor Party leader and Australian Prime Minister BOB HAWKE was born in 1929. He was president of the Australian Council of Trade Unions from 1970 until 1980 before entering politics as the member for Wills. He was prime minister from 1983 until 1991. He announced his retirement from politics in 1992 but has attracted media attention with the release of his memoirs in 1994 and the announcement of his divorce from wife HAZEL in November 1994.
British singer and songwriter JOAN ARMATRADING was born in the Caribbean in 1950. She began recording in England in 1972. Hits included "Love And Affection"(1976) and "Drop The Pilot"(1983).

US singer and keyboard player with the family group the 'OSMONDS', DONNY OSMOND was born in 1957. The group consisted of seven siblings. Their hits included "One Bad Apple"(1971), "Down By The Lazy River"(1972) and "Let Me In"(1973) and DONNY's solo hits included "Sweet And Innocent"(1971), "Go Away Little Girl"(1971), "Puppy Love"(1972), "The Twelfth of Never"(1973) and in 1988 "Soldier of Love".
** EVENTS **
1621 : The first regular theatre in the City of London
was destroyed by fire. It was known as the Fortune Theatre.
1842 : The first Christmas card was created in England.
1917 : The British captured Jerusalem from the Turks.
1925 : The National Opera Trust was formed in the United
Kingdom.
1955 : "SUGAR RAY" ROBINSON regained the world
middleweight boxing crown by knocking out CARL OLSON.
1964 : English poet DAME EDITH SITWELL died. Her work was
often derided in her day but gained popularity later.
1967 : NICHOLAE CEAUSESCU became president of Romania. He

was leader of the Romanian Communist Party which was in power from 1965 until 1989. He was openly critical of the USSR and appointed family members to senior state positions and governed in an increasingly oppressive manner. The CEASESCUS were overthrown in a bloody revolutionary coup in December 1989 and executed. A report smuggled to the United Nations just months earlier accused the CEASESCU regime of widespread human-rights abuses.
1971 : Three hundred children died when Indian planes
bombed an orphanage in the East Pakistan city of Dacca.
1978 : The best pictures ever taken of the planet Venus

were transmitted to earth. Two US Pioneer spacecraft, launched earlier in the year, reached the planet. Pioneer Venus 1 and 2 probed the atmosphere and the surface with radar. The orbiter mapped mountains higher than Everest and the solar system's biggest canyon.
1990 : Solidarity trade union leader LECH WALESA was

elected president of Poland. In the country's first ever direct presidential election came ten years after WALESA led workers in a dispute against the communist regime. He was jailed for nine months and in 1983 was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. In 1988 he again led workers in a wave of industrial action against the government and forced the regime to negotiate. Free elections followed in 1989.
1991 : It was discovered that at least 773 million

dollars was missing from pension funds administered by billionaire ROBERT MAXWELL. AXWELL had died mysterious at sea a month earlier, when he apparently fell from the deck of his luxury yacht. A court order was issued preventing MAXWELL's two sons from leaving England and freezing the assets of KEVIN MAXWELL. This action followed evidence that money continued to be withdrawn from the Mirror Newspaper group's pension fund after MAXWELL's death.
1994 : At least 300 schoolchildren and adults died in a
fire in a cinema in China's north-west.
1994 : The British Government and Sinn Fein, the IRA's
political wing, held their first face-to-face peace talks in the 25 year history of the Northern Ireland conflict.
1994 : The Federal Government passed its sexual-privacy
legislation, aimed at over-riding Tasmania's controversial anti-gay laws.
